svg.title: A 29-byte gzip file from the system's gzip, read by bin/gunzip a field at a time
svg.text: the DEFLATE data, bit by bit in the order read: each byte from its lowest bit up

g.title: The header, 10 bytes: 1f 8b says gzip, 08 says DEFLATE, flags 00 (no name, no comment), the time 0 (none given), 02 (the slowest level), 03 (Unix). The DEFLATE data starts at byte 10.
The block's first 3 bits, read from the lowest bit of byte cb: 1, the last block; then 1, 0, which is the number 1, lowest bit first: a block in the fixed codes.
The next bits, 10011000, are the fixed code of 104, 'h': a literal byte. A code is read a bit at a time until the bits so far are a code (8 here).
The next bits, 10010101, are the fixed code of 101, 'e': a literal byte. A code is read a bit at a time until the bits so far are a code (8 here).
5 more literals, 8 bits each: 'l' 'l' 'o' 'space' 'h'. 7 bytes out so far.
0001000 is symbol 264: a match of length 10. Then a distance: code 4 (00100) and 1 extra bit, 6 back. 10 bytes from 6 back: the copy overlaps the bytes it writes, so it goes a byte at a time.
The next bits, 00111010, are the fixed code of 10, '\n': a literal byte. A code is read a bit at a time until the bits so far are a code (8 here).
0000000 is symbol 256, the end of the block, and the block was the last: 87 bits. The rest of the byte is padding.
The trailer: the CRC-32 of the 18 bytes, df8a7c3b, and their number, 18, each lowest byte first. gunzip works both out from what it wrote; they agree, so it writes the output.
